fields.description:
## Summary

`mutation_sandbox.wrap()` has TWO independent fail-open branches when no OS sandbox
mechanism is available:

1. **ambient `CI` truthy** — proceeds UNSANDBOXED with a warning;
2. **`REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED=1`** — the explicit, documented opt-out.

The first is the problem. `CI` is inheritable and trivially set, so a workstation with
`CI=1` exported — say, while debugging a CI script — silently runs mutation tests with
no sandbox. That is the configuration the 2026-08-26 incident happened in, and nothing
about it is a deliberate choice by the person running the command.

## Approach: remove the branch, do not add a knob

The fix is SUBTRACTIVE. Delete the `CI`-keyed branch, leaving the explicit opt-out as
the single waiver surface. Adding a new config key — as this ticket originally
proposed — would create two overlapping unsandboxed-waiver surfaces with divergent
semantics, which is worse than the gap it closes.

After this, disabling the sandbox requires naming `REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED`,
which is deliberate, greppable, and already documented.

## The lane that relies on the CI branch today

`.github/workflows/_mutation.yml` runs the mutation gate on a plain `ubuntu-latest`
runner. It installs bubblewrap, and its comment claims "Without it the gate fails
CLOSED" — but those runners deny unprivileged `CLONE_NEWUSER`, so `probe()` returns
`None` and **the gate currently runs UNSANDBOXED via the `CI` branch**. The protection
that comment describes does not hold there.

That lane must therefore declare the waiver explicitly before the branch is removed, or
it will start aborting. Making it genuinely sandboxed (as `0d22-f664` did for the
enforcement lane) is the better end state and is tracked separately — this ticket must
not silently convert a working lane into a failing one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The `CI`-keyed fail-open branch is REMOVED from `wrap()`. Ambient `CI` alone can
      no longer disable the sandbox. Verified by a test asserting that with `CI` truthy,
      no mechanism, and no opt-out, `wrap()` raises `SandboxUnavailable`.
- [ ] `REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED` remains the single waiver, unchanged in name
      and semantics. No second opt-in surface is introduced. Verified by a test that the
      opt-out still permits an unsandboxed run and still logs at WARNING.
- [ ] `.github/workflows/_mutation.yml` sets the explicit opt-out, with a comment
      stating that the gate runs UNSANDBOXED there and why, so the exposure is visible
      in a reviewed file rather than implied by an ambient variable. Its stale
      "fails CLOSED" comment is corrected.
- [ ] Every other lane is checked for reliance on the removed branch and shown not to
      need it: the enforcement lane has a working `bwrap` (`0d22-f664`), macOS cells have
      `sandbox-exec`, and the pytest cells only run `@live` tests that skip without a
      mechanism. Verified by naming each lane and its mechanism.

## Definition of Done

- Ambient `CI` alone cannot disable the sandbox, and no new waiver surface exists.
- The one lane that relied on it declares the waiver explicitly instead.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`.

## Notes

Split from `baf9-eea0`, whose plan review refused a criterion claiming to require "more
than ambient CI alone" while verifying only warning text. This ticket's own first review
then corrected its central premise: `CI` was never the SOLE condition — the explicit
opt-out already existed — which is what turned the fix from additive to subtractive.
Discovered from `e668-b496`.
